To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resting state brain network is more efficient and more organized in more intelligent subjects.
the more intelligent the subject is, the more the functional network of his/her brain resembles a small-world brain network, i.e. it exhibits high clustering and short path lengths.
intelligence is associated with a small-world network topology of the functional brain network and the parietal lobe is a key region in this functional brain network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain processes information.
the neural basis of individual differences in human intelligence.
the question of how the human brain processes and integrates information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intelligence is a property of the brain that is related to the functional network organization of the brain and that is reflected by efficient small-world properties of the functional brain network.
the functional brain network of highly intelligent individuals exhibits a more small-world-like topology and a stronger parietal hub than less intelligent individuals.
intelligence is associated with an efficient functional network architecture in the resting state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a neural correlate for intelligence in the resting brain.
intelligence is associated with a more efficient brain.
we found a relationship between the functional brain network and intelligence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to show that a highly efficient functional brain network is associated with high intelligence.
intelligence is related to efficient functional brain network characteristics (high clustering and small path length).
intelligence is associated with a small-world functional network organization.
